recipes.name: Mexican Cornbread II
ingredients_raw: 1 (4 ounce) can diced green chile peppers, drained

steps.text: Preheat oven to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C). Lightly grease a 9x9 inch baking pan.
Place cornmeal mix in a large bowl. Stir in egg, milk, creamed corn, cheese and diced green chile peppers. Spread batter into prepared pan.
Bake in preheated oven for 25 minutes, or until golden brown and cornbread pulls away from sides of pan.

raw_recipe.headline: Mexican Cornbread II
raw_recipe.description: This savory bread is made easy with a shortcut using cornbread mix with creamed corn. Jalapeno peppers and Monterey Jack cheese give this tasty bread an unmistakable South-of-the-Border flair.

review.reviewBody: I used a box of Jiffy Corn Muffin mix and follwed the directions on the box added the remaining ingredients and baked. Was very tasteful. My husband even liked it.

I wanted some Mexican cornbread to go with my Mexican Chicken Chowder tonight, but I didn’t have all the ingredients needed. So I subbed 1 1/4 cups self-rising cornmeal for the package mix, used 8 oz of my fresh creamed corn I had put up in the freezer this summer, and used a combination of cheddar and mozzarella cheeses. I made muffins and they turned out great!

This is very easy and tasty especially at 2am. I use 1 pkg of Mexican cornbread mix, 2/3 cup of milk, 2 teaspoons of sugar, 2 teaspoons of store bought diced jalapenos, and substitute cheese with a Mexican cheese blend. I leave the creme corn out cause well that stuff is just gross. I also use a muffin/cupcake pan in order to make individual servings easier plus it looks cool when it's done. I have also made this with 6oz of crab meat added in.

This mexican cornbread was very good. I was baking it to go with my blackeyed peas and ham on New Years Day so I doubled the recipe. The only thing was I only added one can of the chile peppers because I was afraid it would be too much heat - no it would have been fine with two cans. Also when I baked it I used the cornstick iron skillet and the small iron skillet and put a little extra cheese on top at the end of baking. It turned out perfect, moist and tender on the inside and super crunchy on the outside - with a great kick but could have used a little more heat if I had the guts and added the 2nd can of chilis. This was gone the same day even though I was hoping to take some to work.

For those who ended up with soggy, mushy cornbread, you may have added too much cream-style corn. The recipe calls for an 8 oz. can, which I've never seen in the stores. I've always bought a 14 oz. can. I used approximately half of a 14 oz. can. I also used a Jiffy corn muffin mix, which happens to weigh 8.5 oz. I believe that this is what the recipe submitter intended since the directions mentions cornmeal mix. I followed the directions on the back of the package (1/3 cup milk and 1 egg) and then added the corn, pepper-Jack cheese, and green chiles. 1/2 cup of milk would be too much. No added sugar needed if using the Jiffy mix since it is plenty sweet. Moist but still able to eat with hands.

Pretty good recipe, except I found the green chiles to be overwhelming. Either halve the can of chiles, or double all other ingredients. Since my daughter has Celiac, I use a copycat jiffy mix recipe and replace wheat flour with masa harina corn flour. I recommend everyone try this - you still get the fluffy texture with a corn flavor punch. The cheese is optional, fyi.

I have made this many times and it's always a hit. I usually add a small can of sliced black olives and a little cumin and chili powder. As other reviewers have said, I use a packaged corn muffin mix and add the egg and amount of milk recommended on the package (1/3 cup). Sometimes I use pepper jack cheese instead of plain jack to add a little more spice.

Another 5 star recipe! I added 2 tablespoons of sugar and used a small amount of chopped jalapeños in lieu of the green chilies. Served it alongside Allrecipes Slow Cooker Chicken Taco Soup and these two items together turned a simple, easy dinner into something that totally impressed the fam bam. Thank you!!!

I'm glad I read the review about the creamed corn. I would have dumped the whole can in there. It calls for 8 oz., but a regular sized can is 14.5 oz. I also replaced the green chiles with canned jalapeños, and used hot pepper blend cheese. It has some kick! But, I like that & I think my changes made it perfect. I'll be serving it with Mexican beef stew.
Made this to go with chili tonight. My cornbread mix was 16oz so I doubled other ingredients and used a full size can creamed corn. It turned out really tasty and made a loaf plus 12 muffins.

This was DELICIOUS! I could have skipped the soup I made to go along with this and eaten as it as meal (you know...a very unbalanced one ;). I used a box of Jiffy cornbread mix and a combination of cheddar and mozzarella, since that's what I had on hand. Also sprinkled some extra cheddar on top for the last 5 min or so. This comes out super moist and very flavorful without being very spicy. A new favorite in our home to be sure!

Easy to mix . Simple to freeze . Most items are the ones you have anyway. I always make an extra pan of cornbread and cut in pieces so it is to grab enough for me and still have some for later. If you do not have fresh peppers & you did not freeze a few for later then use canned ones.

This is so good! Easy, quick, moist, and yummy! I made it exactly as recipe. I also made Kansas Baked Beans for the first time and served it over this cornbread. My husband couldn't stop telling me how great it was... especially with the combo with the beans.

I made this according to the recipe EXCEPT I substituted some diced jalapeños from a jar because I didn’t have a can of green chiles. The flavor is good. It took a bit longer to cook- about 30 minutes- and it was still a bit pudding-y. I’d give it 4.5 stars if I could to a half- I’ll make it again.
The texture and flavor was good but I would double on the cream style corn to make the taste a little softer. It tasted like it could use a little more sweetness.

Cornbread always seems a little dry and crumbly to me...until now! I made the recipe as written except I added slightly more creamed corn than was called for, and it was fantastic. My son, who dislikes cornbread, said it was really moist and tasty. Thanks for a great keeper of a recipe.
Followed recipe exactly. Real moist

We liked this. It has somewhat of a "pudding" texture." It's very moist, but it tastes good. As suggested in some of the reviews, I used a box of Jiffy corn muffin mix and used only 1/3 c milk as indicated on the Jiffy box.
So yummy. Everyone loved it!

Made it exactly the way the recipe indicated and it was delicious. I've never had a cornbread recipe that did not use lard or bacon grease come out this moist. Make sure you read the recipe correctly - it does not call for the entire can of creamed corn! I think some of the folks who have not had success are probably using the whole can.
